text:
lee: hi all, day 2 and hit a weird one. company-provided Linux laptop (Ubuntu 22.04) on home network. Okta installed WireGuard, shows handshake, but internal hostnames (artifacts.internal, prometheus:9090) fail to resolve. `ping 10.50.5.10` times out. i can SSH to bastion but proxying attempts stall. who should I tag?

harper: welcome @lee! quick diagnostics: `ip route`, `wg show`, and `systemd-resolve --status` please. Also, sometimes NetworkManager doesn't accept routes from the WireGuard profile; check `nmcli connection show --active`.

lee: ip route shows default via 192.168.0.1 and no 10.50 route. `wg show` has latest handshake, AllowedIPs includes 10.50.0.0/16. `nmcli` shows wireguard connection active. `systemd-resolve --status` lists only 1.1.1.1 and my home DNS.

harper: ok that points to routes not being applied despite the connection. Two quick workarounds: 1) use `ssh -D 1080 -p 443 lee@bastion.corp.redwood.com` and set `ALL_PROXY=socks5://localhost:1080` for cli tools; 2) add the missing route manually: `sudo ip route add 10.50.0.0/16 dev wg0` (replace wg0 with your interface). If ip route add is refused, your distro may have policykit blocking it.

lee: tried manual `ip route add` and it allowed it. after adding route ping to 10.50.5.10 works but HTTP hostnames still fail to resolve.

harper: DNS still going to ISP; the WireGuard config should push a DNS server (10.50.1.2). if nm didn't pick it up you can add `nameserver 10.50.1.2` to `/etc/resolv.conf` temporarily or use `resolvectl dns wg0 10.50.1.2`. Be careful: NetworkManager might overwrite it on reconnect.

lee: did `sudo resolvectl dns wg0 10.50.1.2` and now internal hostnames resolve. thanks!

infra-oncall: logging INFRA-10221 to track this pattern. We're seeing a handful of Ubuntu 22.04 devices where NetworkManager ignores DNS from Okta-WG profiles. We'll push a config tweak to the onboarding profile to set `DNS=10.50.1.2` in the systemd-resolved hook. In the meantime, if anyone else hits this, try `resolvectl` or the ssh socks proxy workaround.

it-bot: device policy check: lee's device is approved; no MDM restrictions detected. Bastion certificate valid.

courtney: welcome @lee :tada: — if you want I can pair for 30m to get your git credentials and dotfiles synced now that networking is sorted.

lee: that would be awesome, thanks everyone! saved my setup flow for the week. :)
